basic_info.name: NRCeS OPConsultRecord - FHIR Implementation Guide for ABDM
basic_info.description: OPConsultRecord is the canonical physician-facing outpatient consultation-summary contract in the FHIR Implementation Guide for ABDM published by NRCeS (National Resource Centre for EHR Standards, C-DAC Pune) for the National Health Authority. It is a FHIR R4 Composition profile whose Composition.type is fixed to SNOMED CT 371530004 'Clinical consultation report', whose mandatory elements are status, type, subject (Patient), encounter, date, author and title, and whose section is sliced (Unordered, Open At End) into 12 fixed SNOMED-coded section slices (ChiefComplaints, PhysicalExamination, Allergies, MedicalHistory, FamilyHistory, InvestigationAdvice, Medications, FollowUp, Procedure, Referral, OtherObservations, DocumentReference). It is instantiated inside a DocumentBundle as Bundle.type=document with the Composition as the first entry. Version verification for this sweep: the current PUBLISHED version is v6.5.0 (package ndhm.in#6.5.0, generated 2025-05-08, marked 'current published version'); v7.0.0 is only a 'Local Development build' preview (draft as of 2026-07-15, package ndhm.in#7.0.0) that does NOT change OPConsultRecord's type or its 12 section codes but introduces a major new Indian Patient Summary (INPS) profile family derived from HL7 IPS 2.0.0, plus WellnessRecord and ImmunizationRecord. The most load-bearing fact for MediKiosk: OPConsultRecord is the exact artifact Module C must emit, but it is explicitly a doctor-authored consult note with no HPI, no review-of-systems, no social-history and no AYUSH (Prakriti/Vikriti) sections, so a pre-visit, patient-elicited, AYUSH-aware summary has to be mapped onto these 12 slices (or the new INPS) rather than emitted natively.
basic_info.organization: Published by the National Resource Centre for EHR Standards (NRCeS), C-DAC Pune, for the National Health Authority (NHA) under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), Government of India; package namespace ndhm.in. The IG is derived from the ABDM Health Data Interchange Specifications 1.0.
basic_info.status: production (v6.5.0 is the current published, 'active' release, package ndhm.in#6.5.0, generated 2025-05-08; v7.0.0 exists only as a preview/'Local Development build' and is not the published version)

technical_features.what_it_does: Defines the minimum conformance requirements for a shareable outpatient (OP) consultation note in the Indian ABDM ecosystem. A conformant OPConsultRecord is a FHIR R4 Composition that logically packages the clinical content of an OP visit - chief complaints, physical examination, allergies, medical history, family history, investigation advice, medications, follow-up, procedures, referrals, other observations and supporting documents - so it can be exchanged across the health ecosystem. It is the physician-authored consult-note contract (NHA/NRCeS), distinct from HealthDocumentRecord (patient-uploaded unstructured documents), PrescriptionRecord, DischargeSummaryRecord, DiagnosticReportRecord, and (in v7.0.0) the Indian Patient Summary. For MediKiosk it is the target output contract for Module C's 'structured, physician-ready summary', with the caveat that it is designed around a clinician's post-exam note.
technical_features.architecture: A StructureDefinition (profile) on the FHIR R4 Composition resource, layered on the generic Composition and constrained by ABDM's mandatory/must-support/fixed-value rules. The Composition must be assembled into a document Bundle: per the DocumentBundle profile the Composition is the first entry (entry[0]) and every referenced resource (Patient, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Organization, Encounter, Condition, Observation, AllergyIntolerance, FamilyMemberHistory, ServiceRequest, MedicationStatement/MedicationRequest, Procedure, Appointment, DocumentReference, Clinic, etc.) is a subsequent entry in the same Bundle with Bundle.type=document. The IG is distributed as an NPM package (ndhm.in) with structure definitions, value sets and examples, so it can be loaded into FHIR validators/tooling. As a standard it has no runtime/algorithm - it is a validation and interchange contract.
technical_features.inputs: Not applicable in the ML sense - it is a data contract, not a system. In use, a conformant instance is populated from a clinician's consult encounter: patient history elicited during the consult, examination findings and vitals, diagnoses/conditions, allergies, medications prescribed or taken, investigation orders, procedures, follow-up plans, referrals, and scanned/attached documents. MediKiosk's Module C would populate it from the Module A conversational history bundle plus Module B digitised-document FHIR extracts, plus the physician's attestation.
technical_features.outputs: A FHIR R4 document: a Bundle of type 'document' whose entry[0] is an OPConsultRecord Composition (type fixed SNOMED CT 371530004 'Clinical consultation report'), with the 12 SNOMED-coded section slices referencing standard FHIR resources, plus a mandatory Composition.attester slot for accuracy attestation and an optional custodian. Every resource is expected to carry its NRCeS profile URL in meta.profile. It is exchanged as a JSON/XML Bundle (not a free-text note).
technical_features.standards_compliance: The conformance contract itself, and it is explicit rather than claimed. Base standard: HL7 FHIR R4 (4.0.1). Terminology: SNOMED CT for Composition.type and all section codes (system http://snomed.info/sct), with value sets for other elements (e.g. CompositionStatus required binding; FHIRDocumentTypeCodes preferred for type; DocumentSectionCodes example binding for section.code). ABDM-specific profiles govern the referenced resources (Patient, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Organization, Encounter, Condition, Observation, AllergyIntolerance, FamilyMemberHistory, ServiceRequest, MedicationStatement, MedicationRequest, Procedure, Appointment, DocumentReference, DocumentBundle). Fixed values in v6.5.0: type.coding.system=http://snomed.info/sct, type.coding.code=371530004, type.coding.display='Clinical consultation report'. Section fixed codes (verified in both v6.5.0 and v7.0.0 preview): ChiefComplaints 422843007 'Chief complaint section'; PhysicalExamination 425044008 'Physical exam section'; Allergies 722446000 'Allergy record'; MedicalHistory 371529009 'History and physical report'; FamilyHistory 422432008 'Family history section'; InvestigationAdvice 721963009 'Order document'; Medications 721912009 'Medication summary document'; FollowUp 390906007 'Follow-up encounter'; Procedure 371525003 'Clinical procedure report'; Referral 306206005 'Referral to service'; OtherObservations 404684003 'Clinical finding'; DocumentReference 371530004 'Clinical consultation report'. Constraints: cmp-1 (each section must contain text, entry or sub-section), cmp-2 (emptyReason only if empty), plus FHIR dom-2..dom-6. No LOINC/ICD/ICD-11 or AYUSH/NAMASTE sections are defined by OPConsultRecord itself. Conformance is intended to be machine-validated (e.g. HAPI FHIR / the ndhm.in package), not merely asserted.
technical_features.offline_capability: Not applicable - OPConsultRecord is a static data contract with no runtime and therefore no intrinsic connectivity requirement. Offline behaviour is entirely a property of the emitting system: MediKiosk can build and validate the Bundle offline and store/store-and-forward it, because FHIR R4 document Bundles are self-contained and the ndhm.in package can be embedded locally. The relevant practical point is that the contract imposes no server dependency for construction, which suits the kiosk's offline-first constraint.
technical_features.languages_supported: The contract is language-neutral: FHIR string/narrative fields can carry any Unicode text, so a bilingual (Hindi/Devanagari plus English) narrative summary is technically emittable. However, the profile's codings are SNOMED CT (English concept labels) and it defines no Indic/Devanagari binding, no language-tagged narrative requirements, and no AYUSH/NAMASTE terminology sections. There is no explicit guidance or validation for code-mixed Hinglish. The language question is therefore a design decision for the emitter, not something the standard solves [uncertain].
technical_features.deployment_model: Vendor-neutral interchange standard: any system (HIS, EHR, PHR, kiosk, gateway) that can produce/consume FHIR R4 documents can implement it. In ABDM, producing/dispatching a consult record is the role of a Health Information Provider (HIP) - typically the hospital's compliant software - and consumption is the Health Information User (HIU) with patient consent, mediated through the ABDM gateway and Health Lockers. The IG supplies an NPM package (ndhm.in) that runs inside local validators such as HAPI FHIR, so validation can be performed on-premise/machine-side with no forced cloud dependency.

performance_metrics.accuracy_or_quality_metrics: No accuracy metric applies to a specification. The relevant quantitative facts are conformance-shape numbers: the v6.5.0 OPConsultRecord profile states 'Mandatory: 8 elements (30 nested mandatory elements), Must-Support: 40 elements, Fixed Value: 33 elements' (the '8 mandatory' includes status, type, type.coding.system/code/display, subject.reference, encounter, date, author.reference and title), and it defines 12 section slices (each 0..1) with Composition.section cardinality 1..*. Third-party implementation guidance (Nirmitee) reports that a typical OPConsultation Bundle contains 13 resources and that the common failure modes are: the Composition not being entry[0] (gateway rejection), missing meta.profile on referenced resources (silent validation failure), and wrong Composition.type SNOMED code (type-mismatch errors). These are secondary-source implementation warnings, not NRCeS-stated metrics [uncertain].
performance_metrics.latency: Not applicable to a specification. Bundle construction and local validation cost depends entirely on the emitter; the ndhm.in package loaded into a local HAPI validator can validate a document Bundle in well under a second on commodity CPU, which is compatible with the kiosk's CPU-only budget [uncertain - not separately benchmarked for this sweep].
performance_metrics.resource_requirements: Not applicable - no runtime. Practically, profile validation requires a FHIR validator plus the ndhm.in package (v6.5.0 = package ndhm.in#6.5.0). This is a small text/JSON artifact well within a ~4GB CPU/iGPU kiosk footprint; primary risk is the JVM footprint of HAPI FHIR if a full Java validator is required, versus the lighter fhir.resources structural validation path already used by Module C [uncertain].
performance_metrics.scale_metrics: Not applicable in the adoption sense. Ecosystem context: ABDM is India's national digital-health mission, NHA-operated, under MoHFW; NRCeS publishes/mantains the IG and is also the SNOMED CT National Release Centre. The IG has a public feedback form and versioned releases; the v6.5.0 package and full JSON/XML definitions are downloadable. No published number of live OPConsultRecord bundles emitted in production was found this sweep [uncertain].
performance_metrics.evaluation_protocol: No evaluation protocol - it is a normative specification. 'Evaluation' means validating emitted instances against the profile using a FHIR validator with the ndhm.in package (and, for v7.0.0 INPS, dual ABDM+IPS conformance enforced via the imposeProfile extension at validation time). The IG itself is versioned and published with release notes/QA reports; changes are made through NRCeS, not through a metric-based evaluation. Any MediKiosk claim of conformance must therefore be demonstrated by machine validation against the pinned package version, not asserted.

milestone_significance.relevance_to_module_c: This is the target output contract for Module C and the single most important external interface decision in the project. It converts Module C's job from 'write a good summary' into 'populate a fixed, machine-validatable document so the hospital HIS and the ABDM ecosystem accept it'. It defines: the exact composition type tag (SNOMED 371530004), the mandatory metadata that forces correct attribution and encounter context (status, subject, encounter, date, author, title), the attester slot that implements physician attestation, and the fixed SNOMED section codes that determine where each elicited datum may legally sit. It also caps what can be expressed: because OPConsultRecord has no HPI, ROS, Social History or AYUSH sections, Module C must map SOCRATES/Dashavidha content onto the 12 slices - most likely ChiefComplaints (Condition), MedicalHistory (Condition/Procedure), OtherObservations (Observation, 'Clinical finding') for ROS/other findings, FamilyHistory (FamilyMemberHistory), Allergies, and Medications - and must consciously omit or relocate anything with no honest slot. The v7.0.0-preview Indian Patient Summary (INPS) is a critical secondary signal: NRCeS now defines an IPS-derived patient-summary artifact with Social History, Patient Story, Vital Signs and Plan-of-Care sections, which is the closest thing to a sanctioned 'patient summary' and is directly relevant to the open question of which ABDM artifact should carry a pre-visit, patient-elicited summary.
milestone_significance.what_to_adopt_or_reject: Adopt: (a) emit a real FHIR R4 document Bundle with the OPConsultRecord Composition as entry[0] and every referenced resource carrying its NRCeS meta.profile - the contract is the market; (b) pin to the current published package, ndhm.in#6.5.0, and machine-validate every emitted Bundle in CI/eval (do not claim conformance without validation); (c) use the exact fixed SNOMED codes verbatim (type 371530004; the 12 verified section codes) rather than inventing or paraphrasing; (d) populate the attester slot (Composition.attester, mode 1..1 bound to personal|professional|legal|official, party reference to the Practitioner/PractitionerRole) as the machine representation of physician attestation - the natural anchor for MediKiosk's 'physician attestation' constraint; (e) emit only data-backed sections and use the standard emptyReason/text semantics for genuinely absent data rather than fabricating; (f) track v7.0.0/INPS for the eventual patient-summary artifact. Reject/defer: (a) inventing an HPI or ROS section code - there is none, so map honestly to OtherObservations/ChiefComplaints/MedicalHistory or omit; (b) pretending AYUSH content (Prakriti, Vikriti) has a home in OPConsultRecord - it does not, so AYUSH output must either live in narrative text, in a separate AYUSH/NAMASTE artifact, or await an NRCeS AYUSH profile; (c) writing outside the fixed section whitelist (open-at-end slicing allows extra sections, but judges/NRCeS will treat non-SNOMED section codes as non-conformant); (d) assuming the attester is mandatory - it is 0..* (must-support), so if attestation is a product requirement MediKiosk must enforce it at the application layer, not rely on the profile.
milestone_significance.limitations_and_risks: Corrections and caveats found during verification. (1) The task brief described OPConsultRecord as having 'a mandatory attester slot' - this is INCORRECT for v6.5.0: Composition.attester is 0..* (must-support flag 'S', not 1..1). Attestation is therefore an application-level requirement MediKiosk must enforce itself, not something the profile guarantees. (2) The brief also implied v6.5.0 is current and v7.0.0 'in preview' - confirmed, with the nuance that v7.0.0 is a 'Local Development build' (draft 2026-07-15), not a published release, so emitters must pin to ndhm.in#6.5.0. (3) The description's '12 SNOMED-sliced sections' is confirmed exactly, and all 12 codes were re-verified against both versions (they are unchanged in v7.0.0). (4) OPConsultRecord is the DOCTOR's consult note: it has no explicit HPI, ROS, Social History, pregnancy or AYUSH sections, so it is an imperfect container for a patient-elicited pre-visit history - the mapping is lossy by design and is a genuine, citable limitation, not just an implementation detail. (5) The open question 'which ABDM artifact carries the kiosk-generated pre-visit summary?' gains a new candidate in v7.0.0 (INPS), but INPS is preview-only and would introduce dual ABDM+IPS conformance and mandatory Problems/Allergies/Medication sections that a history-taking (not diagnosing) kiosk may not always be able to populate; no NRCeS profile yet exists that is explicitly for patient-elicited summaries. (6) Bundle-integration failure modes (Composition not entry[0]; missing meta.profile) are third-party-reported, not NRCeS-stated, and should be confirmed against the ndhm.in package before being treated as hard rules [uncertain]. (7) There is no publicly stated deadline for v7.0.0 becoming the published version, so the emitter must be built with a version switch and re-swept before lock.
milestone_significance.differentiator_vs_medikiosk: This item is not a competitor - it is the substrate MediKiosk differentiates on. Most rivals either do not emit a national-FHIR-IG document at all (MiiHealth DAINA writes HL7v2 into EHR fields; ambient scribes write EHR-native notes) or emit only 'FHIR-shaped' summaries without profile validation (the competing SIH26047 repo). MediKiosk's differentiator is precisely that it emits a physician-attested, NRCeS-OPConsultRecord-conformant document Bundle built offline and on-device. Conforming to this contract strengthens MediKiosk's positioning and is hard to replicate without deep FHIR work. The risks it creates are (a) conformance is unforgiving - a single wrong fixed code or a missing meta.profile fails validation, so the emitter must be tested against the real package; (b) the contract's lack of HPI/ROS/AYUSH sections constrains how much of MediKiosk's clinical value can be represented structurally, so the bilingual narrative and AYUSH layer need a deliberate home; and (c) if NRCeS ships the INPS profile broadly, the 'patient summary' artifact becomes standardised and a generic kiosk could converge on it, slightly eroding uniqueness - though dual ABDM+IPS conformance and the mandatory-section requirements raise the bar. Net: it strongly strengthens MediKiosk's differentiation, provided the emitter is genuinely validated and does not overclaim.

business_info.license: Government-published normative specification, freely available for implementation. NRCeS distributes the IG package (ndhm.in) and downloadable definitions; the IG footer references CC0 for the publication. Note: using SNOMED CT codes requires an SNOMED CT India affiliate licence (free for use within India via MLDS, with sublicensing/reporting obligations), and using the NRCeS profiles does not itself confer any licence to third-party terminologies beyond their own terms.
business_info.pricing: Free to use - it is a national standard published by a government body (NHA/MoHFW via NRCeS). No licence fee for the specification; the cost is in implementation, validation tooling, and (where applicable) terminology-affiliate compliance.
business_info.funding: Funded as public infrastructure: NRCeS (C-DAC Pune) is established for the Government of India under MoHFW, and the IG is maintained for the National Health Authority (NHA) in support of ABDM. Not a commercial venture; no venture funding.
business_info.commercial_status: Government programme / national standard (not a commercial product or paid service). Maintained by a government standards body, with a public feedback form and versioned releases.

competition_ecosystem.competitors: As a standard, not a competitor to itself; the relevant alternatives/analogues are other summary contracts and profiles in the same space: (a) within the same NRCeS IG - HealthDocumentRecord (patient-uploaded unstructured documents), PrescriptionRecord, DischargeSummaryRecord, DiagnosticReportRecord, ImmunizationRecord and WellnessRecord (the last two added in v7.0.0), plus DocumentBundle; (b) the new NRCeS Indian Patient Summary (INPS), derived from HL7 IPS 2.0.0 (v7.0.0 preview), which is the nearest rival artifact for a patient-summary use case; (c) international - HL7 International Patient Summary (IPS) / ISO 27269, and US Core (FHIR R4) document summaries; (d) 'FHIR-shaped' but non-validated outputs from commercial tools and the competing SIH26047 repo, which are not true profile-conformant competitors.
competition_ecosystem.integrations: ABDM gateway roles: the record is produced by a HIP (Health Information Provider - typically the hospital's compliant software/HIS) and consumed by an HIU (Health Information User) under patient consent; Health Lockers store patient records. The bundle references standard ABDM-profiled resources (Patient, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Organization, Encounter, Condition, Observation, AllergyIntolerance, FamilyMemberHistory, ServiceRequest, MedicationStatement/MedicationRequest, Procedure, Appointment, DocumentReference) and the DocumentBundle. Tooling integrations: validators that load the ndhm.in package (e.g. HAPI FHIR and the ABDM sandbox), and the NHCX (National Health Claims Exchange) profile set which shares the same IG. No messaging/telemetry integration (standalone standard).
competition_ecosystem.ecosystem_notes: ABDM is a national government programme (MoHFW/NHA) and NRCeS is also India's SNOMED CT National Release Centre, so this contract carries regulatory-tailwind weight: aligning Module C to it is procurement- and policy-positive for an Ayush/AIIA-adjacent kiosk. Two ecosystem facts matter for planning: (1) v7.0.0 is actively adding patient-summary (INPS) and wellness/immunization profiles and appears to be moving toward dual ABDM+IPS conformance, so the target contract is evolving and the emitter must be version-aware; (2) because both the consult-note contract (OPConsultRecord) and the document-upload contract (HealthDocumentRecord) already exist but neither is explicitly a patient-elicited pre-visit summary, there is a live standards gap that MediKiosk can either fill with a documented mapping or influence via NRCeS feedback - and the v7.0.0 INPS 'Patient Story' section suggests NRCeS is at least moving toward patient-authored content.

history.release_date: The profile's page carries 'Draft as of 2020-09-17' (the original NDHM-era draft lineage). The current PUBLISHED IG version, v6.5.0 (package ndhm.in#6.5.0), was generated/released on 2025-05-08. The v7.0.0 preview build is 'Draft as of 2026-07-15' and was generated on 2026-07-15.
key_milestones: 2020-09-17 - OPConsultRecord profile draft lineage begins under NDHM (predecessor of ABDM).
Earlier published versions in the IG history include v1.2 and v2.0.1 (National Resource Center for EHR Standards / CI build), through v4.0.0.
2025-05-08 - FHIR IG for ABDM v6.5.0 (package ndhm.in#6.5.0) generated and marked the 'current published version' with OPConsultRecord type SNOMED 371530004 and 12 section slices.
2026-02-13 - INPS profile pages show draft dates around this period (e.g. INPS Patient 'Draft as of 2026-02-13'), indicating active patient-summary development.

2026-07-15 - v7.0.0 'Local Development build' generated: adds the Indian Patient Summary (INPS) family derived from HL7 IPS 2.0.0, plus ImmunizationRecord and WellnessRecord; OPConsultRecord's type and 12 section codes unchanged.
history.recent_changes_last_6_months: Within the last 6 months the significant change is the emergence of the v7.0.0 preview build (draft/generated 2026-07-15), which is a substantial expansion of the IG even though it is not yet published. Specifically: (1) it introduces the Indian Patient Summary (INPS) profile family - an implementable FHIR specification derived from the International Patient Summary (IPS) version 2.0.0 (HL7/ISO 27269), with ~25 INPS profiles (Composition, Bundle, Condition, AllergyIntolerance, MedicationStatement/Request, Immunization, Observation results, DiagnosticReport lab/radiology, Procedure, Device, Vital Signs, Social History, Pregnancy, Flag/Alert, Patient Story, CarePlan, etc.); (2) INPS enforces dual conformance to both ABDM base profiles and IPS via the imposeProfile extension, with mandatory sections Problem List, Allergies and Intolerances, Medication Summary, recommended sections Immunizations, Diagnostic Results, History of Procedures and Medical Devices, and optional sections including Patient Story, Social History, Vital Signs, Plan of Care and History of Pregnancy; (3) the IG adds ImmunizationRecord and WellnessRecord clinical-artifact profiles; (4) OPConsultRecord itself is unchanged - the 12 slices and all fixed SNOMED codes (type 371530004; ChiefComplaints 422843007; PhysicalExamination 425044008; Allergies 722446000; MedicalHistory 371529009; FamilyHistory 422432008; InvestigationAdvice 721963009; Medications 721912009; FollowUp 390906007; Procedure 371525003; Referral 306206005; OtherObservations 404684003; DocumentReference 371530004) were re-verified identical in the preview. The v7.0.0 build remains a preview, so the emitted contract for MediKiosk stays pinned to v6.5.0 today. No confirmed date for v7.0.0 publication was found; the public version-history page returned 'TBD'. The v7.0.0 'Generated' date renders as 2026-07-15 on the live pages (some cached/search copies show 2026-02-13); both point to an in-flight preview build rather than a published release.

market_positioning.target_users: Implementers across the Indian digital-health ecosystem: hospital HIS/EHR vendors and health systems (as HIPs), PHR/health-locker and HIU applications, lab/imaging and clinic software, ABDM integrators, and any product that must exchange a standard outpatient consultation summary. Indirectly, NHA and MoHFW policy implementers. For MediKiosk, the target user of the contract is Module C (the emitter) and the hospital HIS/ABDM gateway (the consumer).
market_positioning.market_segment: National health-data-interoperability standard / FHIR implementation guide (ABDM output contract) - specifically the outpatient consult-note artifact. It is not a product, not an ML tool, and not a benchmark; it sits in the FHIR-tooling and standards-compliance segment.
market_positioning.positioning_statement: NRCeS positions the IG as defining 'the minimum conformance requirements for accessing health data to achieve continuity of care in the Indian context', based on FHIR R4 and the ABDM Health Data Interchange Specifications 1.0. OPConsultRecord is presented as 'the outpatient visit consultation note which may include clinical information on any OP examinations, procedures along with medication administered, and advice that can be shared across the health ecosystem', with the profile explicitly setting 'minimum expectations ... to logically package and provide a single coherent statement of meaning, establish its own context that has clinical attestation for a clinical record' and identifying 'the mandatory core elements, vocabularies and value sets which SHALL be present'.
